concept: EmptyState is the printing a room or a list shows before it holds anything, with one line that says what is missing, one sentence of what to do, one key, and at most a quiet drawing made of the system's own unlit parts.

default_to_avoid.pattern: empty state with a big grey stock illustration, a headline, a body paragraph and two buttons, all centred
default_to_avoid.why_not: An illustration is a second voice the case does not have, and two buttons give an empty room two loud answers where P1 allows one.

default_to_avoid.pattern: empty state that only says No data with nothing to do next
default_to_avoid.why_not: A blank message leaves the person stuck; the sentence under the line must say what to do to fill the room.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): an unlit scale and an empty band window before the set is tuned
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): a display that shows a dash pattern when it holds no reading
Nielsen Norman Group, Designing Empty States in Complex Applications (2020): say why it is empty and how to fill it

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The line, the sentence and the key are start-aligned on the inset line of the room they sit in, never centred in the middle of it.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The key is plastic by default and orange only when filling the room is the screen's one main action.

derivation.consequence: holes are ink at a lower step
derivation.form: The grille drawing is a field of unlit holes at the lower ink step, the meter of a room with nothing in it.
The display drawing is an LCD window reading two dashes in segments, the reading of a device with no value yet.

options.name: printed on the case, drawing, line, sentence and key start-aligned
empty slot, a dashed outline of the missing unit with the words inside
row form, the drawing at the start and the words beside it

variants.reason: A prints the words on the room's own inset line in reading order and needs no new edge or layout (P5); B adds a dashed rule the case never uses and reads as a drop zone, and C squeezes the words into a narrow column in a phone sized room.

root.why: The parts stack on the inset line of the surface they sit in, so the empty state has no body of its own.

drawing.why: The drawing uses the system's own unlit window or holes, with no gradient, no glow and no picture.

line.why: The line that says what is missing is medium weight at emphasis size, the largest printing here.

say.why: The sentence of what to do is the secondary ink, which holds 4.5:1 on the plastic body.

action.why: The one key sits last in reading order, under the sentence that says what it does.
